country.name: Guatemala
country.languagePolicy: Spanish is the default interface language. Maya, Garífuna and Xinka language access and regional or local curriculum adaptations require review with the responsible MINEDUC authority and affected communities; machine translation is not reviewed localization.

review.policy: No category becomes verified without a named qualified Guatemalan reviewer, a current authoritative source and review of national, departmental, regional, local and institutional authority where applicable.

governanceModel.summary: Guatemala combines MINEDUC authority for non-university education, national, regional and local curriculum implementation, the autonomous Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala, and CEPS authorization of private universities. These responsibilities must not be collapsed into one approval claim.
governanceModel.departmentalAuthorityRule: Record the responsible Dirección Departamental de Educación and regional or local curriculum implementation when applicable.
governanceModel.higherEducationRule: Verify Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala under its autonomous authority and private universities through the Consejo de la Enseñanza Privada Superior.

authorities.name: Ministerio de Educación
authorities.role: national authority for non-university education and authorized schools

authorities.name: Dirección General de Currículo
authorities.role: Currículo Nacional Base and curricular guidance

authorities.name: Consejo de la Enseñanza Privada Superior
authorities.role: authorization and oversight of private universities

authorities.name: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala
Secretaría contra la Violencia Sexual, Explotación y Trata de Personas
authorities.role: prevention and protection authority within its statutory remit, including children and adolescents

curriculum.title: Currículo Nacional Base
curriculum.implementationRule: Confirm the applicable level, modality, ministerial agreement, current guidance and national, regional and local curricular adaptation.
curriculum.supplementPolicy: External materials may supplement but never replace, waive or silently reinterpret the controlling CNB and applicable ministerial requirements.

schoolDirectory.primarySourceName: Búsqueda de centros educativos autorizados por el Mineduc
schoolDirectory.scopeNotice: A center can have multiple codes for authorized services, levels, plans or shifts. BRASA must preserve each code and authorized service and must not turn one code or listing into blanket approval of every program.

publicUniversity.name: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala
publicUniversity.authorityNotice: USAC is constitutionally autonomous; verify programs and credentials directly with its official records.

privateUniversities.authority: Consejo de la Enseñanza Privada Superior
privateUniversities.authorityNotice: CEPS authorizes creation of private universities. Verify the named institution and do not infer a separate program accreditation claim without evidence.

privacyAndSafeguarding.comprehensiveLawNotice: As reviewed on 2026-10-15, congressional sources show proposed comprehensive personal-data legislation still under consideration. BRASA must not claim that a proposal is enacted law and requires country legal review for public and private processing.
privacyAndSafeguarding.scopeNotice: Public-record habeas-data protections, applicable sector rules, child-protection law and institutional consent, safeguarding and incident procedures require review before real learner participation.

completionCriteria: A qualified Guatemalan education reviewer is named.
MINEDUC national, departmental, regional and local implementation boundaries are reviewed.
Every school record preserves each MINEDUC code and the specific authorized service, level, modality and shift.
USAC autonomy and CEPS private-university authority are represented separately.
Every institution, program and credential claim identifies its documentary authority and review date.
CNB mappings identify level, modality, ministerial agreement and applicable regional or local adaptation.
Maya, Garífuna and Xinka language and cultural requirements are reviewed with competent community participation.
The absence or status of comprehensive personal-data legislation is rechecked by qualified counsel before a real pilot.
Privacy, child protection, accessibility, incident and consent procedures are approved by the participating institution.
No authorization, partnership, accreditation or credential claim exceeds documentary evidence.
